<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>I plan to send the same message to everyone in my friend list but I have over 300 friends and it is very hard to do that by hand or with macro.</p>
<p>I am looking for a software that can do that for me, preferably that works with multiple accounts at a time with the option to use proxies.</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm trying to find the last Spirit of Arkham in Batman, Arkham Asylum, but I am totally stumped. I have otherwise completed the game 100% (including the challenges) and this seems to be the last thing left to do.</p>
<p>It seems like I am supposed to find a person and from the previous clues, I am fairly sure that person is</p>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p>Warden Sharp.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>However, I have not seen them in ages and I have no idea where they might be. I feel like I have spent several hours now combing every inch of the island and all of the buildings, spoken to every living person I can find, but no luck.</p>
<p>I would very much prefer a subtle hint, rather than a heavy spoiler, just to set me in the right direction. I have a couple of questions in particular that I would really like answers to, so perhaps we could just start with these for now?:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>What is it I actually need to do, once I find the correct person? Do I just need to talk to them, or is there more required than that?</p>
</li>
<li><p>Am I correct that it is</p>
</li>
</ol>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p>Warden Sharp?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>If so, is there any subtle clue you can give me as to where they can be found?</p>
<p>Thanks in advance (again, please no heavy spoilers)!</p>
</div>

<p>Maybe check the room where you last encountered him?</p>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p> It is in the Central control room (The last place you see the warden) You will see a smaller round room lined with computers on desks, there is also a bunch of writing on the ground all you need to do is scan that room and you've found it.</p>
</blockquote>

        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer

            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm trying to find the last Spirit of Arkham in Batman, Arkham Asylum, but I am totally stumped. I have otherwise completed the game 100% (including the challenges) and this seems to be the last thing left to do.</p>
<p>It seems like I am supposed to find a person and from the previous clues, I am fairly sure that person is</p>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p>Warden Sharp.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>However, I have not seen them in ages and I have no idea where they might be. I feel like I have spent several hours now combing every inch of the island and all of the buildings, spoken to every living person I can find, but no luck.</p>
<p>I would very much prefer a subtle hint, rather than a heavy spoiler, just to set me in the right direction. I have a couple of questions in particular that I would really like answers to, so perhaps we could just start with these for now?:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>What is it I actually need to do, once I find the correct person? Do I just need to talk to them, or is there more required than that?</p>
</li>
<li><p>Am I correct that it is</p>
</li>
</ol>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p>Warden Sharp?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>If so, is there any subtle clue you can give me as to where they can be found?</p>
<p>Thanks in advance (again, please no heavy spoilers)!</p>
</div>

<p>Maybe check the room where you last encountered him?</p>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p> It is in the Central control room (The last place you see the warden) You will see a smaller round room lined with computers on desks, there is also a bunch of writing on the ground all you need to do is scan that room and you've found it.</p>
</blockquote>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm trying to find the last Spirit of Arkham in Batman, Arkham Asylum, but I am totally stumped. I have otherwise completed the game 100% (including the challenges) and this seems to be the last thing left to do.</p>
<p>It seems like I am supposed to find a person and from the previous clues, I am fairly sure that person is</p>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p>Warden Sharp.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>However, I have not seen them in ages and I have no idea where they might be. I feel like I have spent several hours now combing every inch of the island and all of the buildings, spoken to every living person I can find, but no luck.</p>
<p>I would very much prefer a subtle hint, rather than a heavy spoiler, just to set me in the right direction. I have a couple of questions in particular that I would really like answers to, so perhaps we could just start with these for now?:</p>
<ol>
<li><p>What is it I actually need to do, once I find the correct person? Do I just need to talk to them, or is there more required than that?</p>
</li>
<li><p>Am I correct that it is</p>
</li>
</ol>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p>Warden Sharp?</p>
</blockquote>
<p>If so, is there any subtle clue you can give me as to where they can be found?</p>
<p>Thanks in advance (again, please no heavy spoilers)!</p>
</div>

<p>Maybe check the room where you last encountered him?</p>
<blockquote class="spoiler">
<p> It is in the Central control room (The last place you see the warden) You will see a smaller round room lined with computers on desks, there is also a bunch of writing on the ground all you need to do is scan that room and you've found it.</p>
</blockquote>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<p>How do they get those markings, or what is the significance of them?</p>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401507/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>These are clone Pokémon, which were <a href="https://pokemongolive.com/post/pokemonday2020/?hl=en" rel="noreferrer" title="Celebrate Pokémon Day 2020 with Pokémon GO!">available in 4-star raids during Pokémon Day 2020</a>. They are just cosmetic variants of Venusaur, Charizard, Blastoise, and Pikachu.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/YGkgc.jpg" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="Clone Blastoise, Charizard, and Venusaur" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/YGkgc.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>The evolved clone starters came with their respective Community Day charge move, so you can expect them to have it even at low MMR.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>Occasionally I'll face a Charizard or Venusaur in GBL that has dark striping like this:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/8b1m6l.jpg" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/8b1m6l.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>How do they get those markings, or what is the significance of them?</p>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401507/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>These are clone Pokémon, which were <a href="https://pokemongolive.com/post/pokemonday2020/?hl=en" rel="noreferrer" title="Celebrate Pokémon Day 2020 with Pokémon GO!">available in 4-star raids during Pokémon Day 2020</a>. They are just cosmetic variants of Venusaur, Charizard, Blastoise, and Pikachu.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/YGkgc.jpg" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="Clone Blastoise, Charizard, and Venusaur" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/YGkgc.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>The evolved clone starters came with their respective Community Day charge move, so you can expect them to have it even at low MMR.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401507/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>These are clone Pokémon, which were <a href="https://pokemongolive.com/post/pokemonday2020/?hl=en" rel="noreferrer" title="Celebrate Pokémon Day 2020 with Pokémon GO!">available in 4-star raids during Pokémon Day 2020</a>. They are just cosmetic variants of Venusaur, Charizard, Blastoise, and Pikachu.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/YGkgc.jpg" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="Clone Blastoise, Charizard, and Venusaur" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/YGkgc.jpg"/></a></p>
<p>The evolved clone starters came with their respective Community Day charge move, so you can expect them to have it even at low MMR.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401517/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

<span class="comment-copy">@Oddrigue Not entirely. For example, confusion from eating a berry your Pokémon dislikes the taste of relies on the actual nature, not the effect caused by a mint - thus it's better to have a neutral nature (since they like all the flavours) and use a mint to make it the desired nature. You can also never lower IVs - a Trick Room Pokémon wants 0 speed, a special attacker wants 0 attack (in case they get confused and hit themself), etc.</span>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

For example, confusion from eating a berry your Pokémon dislikes the taste of relies on the actual nature, not the effect caused by a mint - thus it's better to have a neutral nature (since they like all the flavours) and use a mint to make it the desired nature. You can also never lower IVs - a Trick Room Pokémon wants 0 speed, a special attacker wants 0 attack (in case they get confused and hit themself), etc.</span>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401517/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

<span class="comment-copy">@Oddrigue Not entirely. For example, confusion from eating a berry your Pokémon dislikes the taste of relies on the actual nature, not the effect caused by a mint - thus it's better to have a neutral nature (since they like all the flavours) and use a mint to make it the desired nature. You can also never lower IVs - a Trick Room Pokémon wants 0 speed, a special attacker wants 0 attack (in case they get confused and hit themself), etc.</span>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

For example, confusion from eating a berry your Pokémon dislikes the taste of relies on the actual nature, not the effect caused by a mint - thus it's better to have a neutral nature (since they like all the flavours) and use a mint to make it the desired nature. You can also never lower IVs - a Trick Room Pokémon wants 0 speed, a special attacker wants 0 attack (in case they get confused and hit themself), etc.</span>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401517/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

<span class="comment-copy">@Oddrigue Not entirely. For example, confusion from eating a berry your Pokémon dislikes the taste of relies on the actual nature, not the effect caused by a mint - thus it's better to have a neutral nature (since they like all the flavours) and use a mint to make it the desired nature. You can also never lower IVs - a Trick Room Pokémon wants 0 speed, a special attacker wants 0 attack (in case they get confused and hit themself), etc.</span>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

For example, confusion from eating a berry your Pokémon dislikes the taste of relies on the actual nature, not the effect caused by a mint - thus it's better to have a neutral nature (since they like all the flavours) and use a mint to make it the desired nature. You can also never lower IVs - a Trick Room Pokémon wants 0 speed, a special attacker wants 0 attack (in case they get confused and hit themself), etc.</span>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

                        Date created (oldest first)
                    </option>
</select>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

                        Date created (oldest first)
                    </option>
</select>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

                        Date created (oldest first)
                    </option>
</select>
</div>
